mainTopic: Repaying for eaten תרומה (by value vs. by measure, and the כזית and פרוטה minimums), and a ברייתא on why intentional מעילה brings no קרבן
overview: אביי explains that רבי עקיבא and רבי יוחנן בן נורי both hold חמץ בפסח is אסור בהנאה. They argue only about how a non-כהן repays for eaten תרומה: by value (worthless חמץ, so nothing owed) or by measure (he returns the same amount). The גמרא proves that רבי יוחנן בן נורי does not follow רבי יוסי הגלילי. A ברייתא then sets the minimum for paying קרן וחומש. The תנא קמא says a כזית, from the word יאכל. אבא שאול says a פרוטה's worth, from the word ונתן. Another ברייתא rules that food worth a פרוטה but smaller than a כזית obligates only the קרן. רב פפא claims this fits אבא שאול, who needs both amounts, but a משנה refutes him with a תיובתא. The גמרא then brings a ברייתא on why intentional מעילה brings no קרבן. רב נחמן בר יצחק says it ranks כרת and מיתה inconsistently. רב חייא בר אבין answers that מעילה is liable even below a כזית, but reports that רבה and רב שׁשת attacked that answer, and their challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: אביי explains what the dispute is really about
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, רבי עקיבא and רבי יוחנן בן נורי all hold חמץ בפסח is אסור בהנאה. רבי עקיבא and רבי יוחנן בן נורי argue only about whether repayment is לפי דמים or לפי מדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, רבי עקיבא and רבי יוחנן בן נורי all hold that חמץ on פסח is forbidden for benefit. They argue about this: רבי עקיבא holds you pay according to value, and רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds you pay according to measure.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains the earlier argument about someone who ate חמץ of תרומה on פסח. He says the argument is not about whether חמץ may be used. It is about how the repayment is calculated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you pay by value (רבי עקיבא), forbidden חמץ is worth nothing, so there is nothing to pay. If you pay by measure (רבי יוחנן בן נורי), you must return the same amount of food, even though the חמץ itself had no value. This lets all three תנאים agree on the איסור הנאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Leavened food during פסח
Forbidden to get any benefit from it
He pays according to the money value
He pays according to the amount or quantity
They disagree

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key idea of the passage: how repayment of תרומה is measured decides whether eating worthless חמץ of תרומה creates any debt.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
phrases.english: Abaye said: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי
phrases.english: and Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri
all of them hold
that chametz on Pesach is forbidden for benefit,
and in this they disagree:

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סָבַר: לְפִי דָמִים מְשַׁלֵּם,
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva holds: he pays according to value,
phrases.notes: Forbidden חמץ has no value, so he pays nothing.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי סָבַר: לְפִי מִדָּה מְשַׁלֵּם.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri holds: he pays according to measure.
phrases.notes: He returns the same quantity, so he must pay even for worthless חמץ.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי כּוּלְּהוּ סְבִירָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the dispute between רבי עקיבא and רבי יוחנן בן נורי quoted earlier on the דף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All three hold חמץ בפסח is אסור בהנאה; רבי עקיבא holds payment is by value, and רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds payment is by measure.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why אביי needed to say this, since it seems like the only possible reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי, saying his explanation seems too obvious to need stating. This sets up the next step, which shows why it was needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumes there is no other reasonable way to read the dispute. The answer will have to show a different reading that someone might have believed.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious; why say it?

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether אביי's statement adds anything new.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If no other reading is reasonable, the statement adds nothing.

steps.title: Why אביי needed to say it
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought רבי יוחנן בן נורי also pays by value. Then he would obligate payment only because he follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, who permits benefit from חמץ. אביי teaches that this is not so.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that רבי יוחנן בן נורי also agrees with רבי עקיבא that you pay by value. In that case, the reason he makes the eater pay is that he follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, who said חמץ on פסח is permitted for benefit. So אביי teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the 'obvious' challenge. It shows another reading of רבי יוחנן בן נורי that אביי wanted to rule out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the alternate reading, both תנאים pay by value. Their only disagreement would be whether חמץ has value, which depends on whether it is מותר בהנאה. אביי rejects this and places the dispute in the method of payment instead.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said
So it teaches us (otherwise)
Permitted for benefit

phrases.english: What might you have said?
that Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri also
holds like Rabbi Akiva,
who said he pays according to value.
And there, this is the reason he obligates payment:

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּסָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי,
phrases.english: because he holds like Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
who said: chametz on Pesach is permitted for benefit,
so he teaches us (that this is not so).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא by showing a possible alternate reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows a reasonable mistaken reading that the statement rules out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן בן נורי pays by value and obligates payment because he holds like רבי יוסי הגלילי that חמץ has value.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds חמץ is אסור בהנאה and obligates payment because payment is by measure.

steps.title: Maybe the alternate reading is actually right
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: why not accept that רבי יוחנן בן נורי really does follow רבי יוסי הגלילי?
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it is indeed so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back and asks why the 'you might have said' reading cannot simply be true. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far, the alternate reading was rejected only by stating אביי's view. Now the גמרא asks for real evidence that רבי יוחנן בן נורי does not hold like רבי יוסי הגלילי.

keyTerms.meaning: But say it is really so

phrases.english: But say it is indeed so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection of the alternate reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוחנן בן נורי does not follow רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No proof has been given that the alternate reading is wrong.

steps.title: Proof: רבי יוחנן בן נורי did not make the dog argument
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יוחנן בן נורי held חמץ is permitted for benefit, he would have answered רבי עקיבא the way רבי אלעזר חסמא answered רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, by pointing out that the חמץ has value. He did not, so he must agree it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, רבי יוחנן בן נורי should have answered רבי עקיבא the same way רבי אלעזר חסמא answered רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that רבי יוחנן בן נורי does not follow רבי יוסי הגלילי. It points to the reply he would have made if he did, and notes that he never made it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר חסמא argued that the חמץ still has value, for example because it can be fed to a dog. If רבי יוחנן בן נורי also thought חמץ has value, that would have been his obvious reply to רבי עקיבא. His silence shows he agrees חמץ is אסור בהנאה, which confirms אביי's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
He should have answered him

steps.whatToRemember: All three תנאים agree חמץ בפסח is אסור בהנאה. The dispute between רבי עקיבא (by value) and רבי יוחנן בן נורי (by measure) is about how תרומה is repaid.

phrases.english: If so,

phrases.aramaic: נַהְדַּר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri should have answered Rabbi Akiva
just as answered him

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר חַסָּמָא לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב.
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar Chisma answered Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov.
phrases.notes: He argued that the חמץ still has value, such as feeding it to a dog.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, נַהְדַּר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge with proof from what רבי יוחנן בן נורי did not say.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from silence: an expected argument was not made
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן בן נורי agrees חמץ is אסור בהנאה; his reason for obligating payment is לפי מדה.

steps.title: Minimum amount for paying for eaten תרומה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: someone who eats a כזית of תרומה pays קרן וחומש. אבא שאול says he pays only if it was worth a פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One who eats a כזית of תרומה pays the principal plus a fifth. אבא שאול says: only if it is worth a פרוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new ברייתא about the minimum amount of eaten תרומה that requires payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא sets the minimum by size, a כזית. אבא שאול sets it by money value, a פרוטה. The two views can differ: a כזית worth less than a פרוטה, or a פרוטה's worth that is smaller than a כזית.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive's volume
The principal plus an added fifth
Worth a פרוטה, the smallest coin
The portion of produce given to a כהן

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who eats an olive-bulk of terumah
pays the principal and a fifth.
Abba Shaul says:
not until it is worth a peruta.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new related topic about paying for eaten תרומה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: a כזית obligates קרן וחומש. אבא שאול: payment requires שוה פרוטה.

steps.title: What is the תנא קמא's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the תנא קמא's כזית standard.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the first תנא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where the תנא קמא gets his כזית rule. This sets up the answer from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question asks why size, not value, would decide whether payment is owed.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
The first, unnamed opinion in the ברייתא

phrases.english: What is the reason of the first tanna?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the opinion just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the כזית minimum

steps.title: The פסוק says eating, and eating means a כזית
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'וְאִישׁ כִּי יֹאכַל קֹדֶשׁ בִּשְׁגָגָה'. The word for eating halachically means a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And if a man eats a holy thing in error', and eating is a כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the תנא קמא's source. The תורה ties the payment to 'eating', and the halachic minimum for eating is a כזית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the obligation depends on an act of אכילה, the תנא קמא uses the size standard of eating. Money value is not the deciding factor in his view.

keyTerms.meaning: And if a man eats a holy thing in error (ויקרא כב:יד)
Eating, halachically a כזית

phrases.english: The verse says:
"And if a man eats a holy thing in error",
and eating is with an olive-bulk.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: ״וְאִישׁ כִּי יֹאכַל קֹדֶשׁ בִּשְׁגָגָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the תנא קמא's source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק uses the word 'eating', and the halachic minimum for eating is a כזית.

steps.title: What is אבא שאול's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of אבא שאול's view that a פרוטה's worth is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אבא שאול, what is his reason?
steps.whatsHappening: Having explained the תנא קמא's source, the גמרא now asks for the source of אבא שאול's view. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבא שאול said one pays קרן וחומש only if the תרומה was worth a פרוטה. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: And Abba Shaul, what is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 7, which asked for the תנא קמא's source. Now the גמרא asks for אבא שאול's.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the שוה פרוטה requirement

steps.title: The word 'and he shall give' requires a פרוטה
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says ונתן, and giving is never less than a שוה פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'and he shall give,' and giving is not less than the value of a פרוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that אבא שאול learns from the word ונתן, meaning 'and he shall give.' Halachically, 'giving' is never less than a פרוטה's worth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא focused on the word for eating, which means a כזית. אבא שאול focuses on the word for giving, which means a פרוטה. Each side reads a different word in the same פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he shall give' (from the פסוק about paying back holy food)
Giving; a halachic act of giving
Worth a פרוטה, the smallest coin of monetary significance

phrases.english: The verse says: "And he shall give,"
and there is no 'giving' of less than a perutah's worth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word ונתן teaches a minimum of שוה פרוטה.

steps.title: But the verse also says 'eats'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אבא שאול: the פסוק also says יאכל, which should require a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for the other one (אבא שאול) too, it is written 'eats'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אבא שאול. The same פסוק uses the word יאכל, which normally means a כזית, so what does he do with it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 showed that 'eating' means a כזית. If אבא שאול ignores that word, he seems to be leaving part of the פסוק unexplained.

keyTerms.meaning: The other one (here, אבא שאול)
'He will eat'

phrases.english: And the other one too,
isn't it written "eats"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אבא שאול using the תנא קמא's word from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: אבא שאול's reading of the פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word יאכל implies a כזית, so what does אבא שאול learn from it?

steps.title: 'Eats' excludes someone who damages
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול uses יאכל to exclude a מזיק from paying the חומש.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word comes to exclude one who damages.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that אבא שאול uses the word יאכל for something else. It teaches that only someone who eats pays the חומש, not someone who merely damages the תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אבא שאול, יאכל teaches the type of act required, namely eating rather than damaging. It does not teach the amount. So it does not set a כזית minimum.

keyTerms.meaning: One who damages, without eating or benefiting
To exclude

phrases.english: That comes to exclude one who damages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redirecting the פסוק to a different teaching
steps.terutzMaskana: For אבא שאול, יאכל excludes a מזיק from the חומש

steps.title: But the verse also says 'and he shall give'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the תנא קמא: what does he do with ונתן?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the תנא קמא: isn't it written 'and he shall give'!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא turns the challenge around. What does the תנא קמא learn from the word ונתן?
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבא שאול learned a פרוטה minimum from ונתן. The תנא קמא does not require a פרוטה, so he needs another use for that word.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: And the first tanna, isn't it written "and he shall give"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror image of step 11, now aimed at the תנא קמא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The תנא קמא's reading of the פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ונתן implies a פרוטה. What does the תנא קמא learn from it?

steps.title: 'And he shall give' requires something fit to be holy
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא uses ונתן to teach that only food fit to become holy is included. This excludes חמץ of תרומה on פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs that word for an item fit to become holy, excluding one who eats תרומה of חמץ on פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the תנא קמא uses ונתן to teach that the food must be fit to be holy. This excludes eating חמץ of תרומה on פסח, which is worthless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The payment must be something that could itself become holy, meaning something of value. חמץ on פסח is forbidden for benefit, so it has no value. Eating it creates no obligation of קרן וחומש. This ties back to the earlier discussion of חמץ of תרומה on פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different teaching)
Something fit to become holy
תרומה of חמץ on פסח, which is worthless

steps.whyThisMatters: This links the derivation back to the main topic of the sugya: eating חמץ of תרומה on פסח.

phrases.english: He needs that
for an item fit to become holy
(to exclude one who eats teruma of chametz on Pesach).

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְדָבָר הָרָאוּי לִהְיוֹת קֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redirecting the פסוק to a different teaching
steps.terutzMaskana: For the תנא קמא, ונתן requires food fit to be holy, which excludes חמץ on פסח

steps.title: Less than a כזית: pay the קרן but not the חומש
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that one who eats less than a כזית of תרומה pays the קרן but not the חומש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: one who eats less than a כזית of תרומה pays the principal but does not pay the fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא. It rules that eating less than a כזית of תרומה obligates only the קרן, not the extra חומש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חומש depends on a halachic act of 'eating,' which requires a כזית. Paying back the קרן is simply repaying what was taken, so it does not depend on the כזית.

keyTerms.meaning: The principal; the base value
The extra fifth added as a penalty

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One who eats less than an olive-bulk of teruma
pays the principal
but does not pay the fifth.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָאוֹכֵל תְּרוּמָה פָּחוֹת מִכְּזַיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a new ברייתא on the same theme of minimum amounts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Less than a כזית obligates קרן but not חומש.

steps.title: What case could this be?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: with or without a פרוטה's worth, the ruling seems not to fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If it is not worth a פרוטה, he should not even pay the principal. If it is worth a פרוטה, he should also pay the fifth!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what case the ברייתא means. Neither possibility seems to fit the ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Below a פרוטה, there is no monetary value, so even the קרן should not be owed. At a פרוטה or more, the גמרא assumes the חומש should also be owed. So the split ruling looks impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case?
If ... and if (a two-sided challenge)

phrases.english: What is the case?
If it is not worth a perutah,
he should not pay the principal either;
and if it is worth a perutah,
he should pay the fifth too!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי? אִי דְּלֵית בֵּיהּ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's split between קרן and חומש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dilemma: without a פרוטה, nothing is owed; with a פרוטה, everything should be owed.

steps.title: Worth a פרוטה but less than a כזית
steps.stepSummary: The case is food worth a פרוטה but smaller than a כזית, so he pays only the קרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It really is worth a פרוטה, and even so, since it is not a כזית, he pays the principal but not the fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the food was worth a פרוטה, which is why the קרן is owed. Because it was less than a כזית, the חומש is not owed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two payments have different requirements. Value of a פרוטה triggers the קרן. The חומש also needs a כזית, because it depends on 'eating.' Small but valuable food meets one requirement and not the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually; really (introduces the true case)
And even so

steps.whatToRemember: The קרן needs a פרוטה's worth. The חומש needs a כזית as well.

phrases.english: Actually, it is worth a perutah,
and even so,
since it is not an olive-bulk,

phrases.aramaic: מְשַׁלֵּם אֶת הַקֶּרֶן וְאֵינוֹ מְשַׁלֵּם אֶת הַחוֹמֶשׁ.
phrases.english: he pays the principal and does not pay the fifth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma of step 16 by choosing the second side.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A פרוטה's worth automatically obligates the חומש
steps.terutzMaskana: A פרוטה obligates the קרן, but the חומש also requires a כזית

steps.title: The רבנן say this ברייתא is not like אבא שאול
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן tell רב פפא that this ברייתא must disagree with אבא שאול, who requires only a פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said before רב פפא: this is not like אבא שאול. If it were, he says that once it is worth a פרוטה, he pays even without a כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן argue that the ברייתא cannot follow אבא שאול. They understand him to obligate full payment whenever there is a פרוטה, even without a כזית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא denies the חומש in a case that has a פרוטה but lacks a כזית. If אבא שאול only cares about a פרוטה, he would require the חומש here. So the רבנן conclude the ברייתא follows the תנא קמא.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן said it before him
Even though

phrases.english: The Sages said before Rav Pappa:
This is not like Abba Shaul,
for if it were like Abba Shaul, he said:
since it is worth a perutah,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֵית בֵּיהּ כְּזַיִת.
phrases.english: even though it is not an olive-bulk.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמְרוּהָ רַבָּנַן קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא הָא דְּלָא כְּאַבָּא שָׁאוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference about whose view the ברייתא of steps 15–17 follows.
steps.raayaObject: The ברייתא follows the תנא קמא, not אבא שאול
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא denies the חומש despite a פרוטה's worth

steps.title: אבא שאול requires both
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rejects the inference: אבא שאול requires both a כזית and a פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to them: you can even say it follows אבא שאול, because אבא שאול requires two things.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא rejects the רבנן's claim. אבא שאול does not replace the כזית with a פרוטה. He adds the פרוטה on top of the כזית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אבא שאול, the חומש needs both a כזית and a פרוטה. So the ברייתא, which denies the חומש without a כזית, fits him too. The two opinions differ only about a כזית worth less than a פרוטה.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say
He requires two things

steps.confusionAlert: Do not treat רב פפא's reading as final. He claims אבא שאול requires both a כזית and a פרוטה, but step 20 attacks this from the משנה, and step 21 rejects it.
steps.whatToRemember: This is only רב פפא's suggestion: that אבא שאול requires both a כזית and a פרוטה. Step 20 challenges it, and step 21 refutes it.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to them:
You may even say it is Abba Shaul;
Abba Shaul requires two things.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְהוּ רַב פָּפָּא: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא אַבָּא שָׁאוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the ברייתא contradicts אבא שאול
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The רבנן assumed אבא שאול replaces the כזית with a פרוטה, when he actually adds it.

steps.title: Does אבא שאול really require two conditions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב פפא from the משנה: אבא שאול mentions only a פרוטה, and the חכמים' reply shows they understood him as not requiring a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does אבא שאול really require two things? But we learned in the משנה: אבא שאול says that if it is worth a פרוטה he must pay, and if it is not worth a פרוטה he does not pay. The חכמים answered him: the פרוטה rule was only said about מעילה, but for תרומה he is not liable until it is a כזית. If רב פפא were right, the חכמים should have said 'since it has a כזית.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב פפא's claim from Step 19 that אבא שאול needs both a כזית and a פרוטה. It quotes the משנה and looks closely at how the חכמים phrased their reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose אבא שאול already required a כזית. Then the only argument between him and the חכמים would be about food that is a כזית but worth less than a פרוטה. In that case the חכמים should have argued 'since there is a כזית, he must pay.' Instead they said 'he is not liable until there is a כזית.' That wording assumes אבא שאול does not require a כזית at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Two (conditions)
Payment / compensation to the כהן
Improper use of הקדש (consecrated property)
And if it were so (as you claim)
He should have said

steps.confusionAlert: The proof does not come from what אבא שאול said. It comes from the wording of the חכמים' reply. 'Not liable until a כזית' shows they understood אבא שאול as satisfied with a פרוטה alone.

phrases.english: And does Abba Shaul really require two (conditions)?
But didn't we learn: Abba Shaul says:
That which has the value of a peruta —
he is liable to pay compensation,
that which does not have the value of a peruta —
he is not liable to pay compensation.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֹא אָמְרוּ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה
phrases.english: They said to him: They did not say 'worth a peruta'
except regarding misuse of consecrated property alone,
but regarding teruma —

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בּוֹ כְּזַיִת.
phrases.english: he is not liable until it contains an olive-bulk.
And if it were so (as Rav Pappa says),
phrases.notes: רב פפא's point is that אבא שאול also requires a כזית.

phrases.english: they should have said, 'Since it contains an olive-bulk.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי בָּעֵי אַבָּא שָׁאוּל תַּרְתֵּי? וְהָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב פפא's דחיה from Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that אבא שאול requires both a כזית and a פרוטה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים' phrasing 'not liable until a כזית' only makes sense if אבא שאול required no כזית. Otherwise they should have argued 'since there is a כזית.'

steps.title: רב פפא is conclusively refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares a תיובתא: רב פפא's reading of אבא שאול is rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules that the challenge cannot be answered, so רב פפא's view is rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With רב פפא refuted, we are back to the רבנן's inference from Step 18. אבא שאול requires only a פרוטה, so the ברייתא from Step 15 does not follow his view.

keyTerms.meaning: A conclusive refutation; the view is rejected

steps.whatToRemember: Final result: אבא שאול requires only a פרוטה, not a כזית. The ברייתא that requires a כזית argues with him.

phrases.english: A conclusive refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the קשיא of Step 20 with no answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב פפא's claim that אבא שאול requires both conditions is rejected.

steps.title: רב פפא also retracted; a ברייתא on intentional מעילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רב פפא himself retracted, and begins citing a ברייתא: 'וחטאה בשגגה' excludes one who sinned במזיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב פפא also took back his view, as it was taught in a ברייתא: 'and he sins by mistake' — this excludes one who did it on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that רב פפא himself changed his mind. It is setting up a ברייתא about מעילה, which the following discussion will connect to רב פפא's retraction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns from the words 'בשגגה' that a קרבן for מעילה applies only to a mistaken act. Someone who misuses הקדש on purpose does not bring this קרבן. The next steps ask why a פסוק is needed for this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He retracted / changed his mind
By mistake, unintentionally
One who acts on purpose
To exclude

phrases.english: And Rav Pappa also retracted,
as it was taught: 'And sins through error' —
phrases.notes: ויקרא ה:טו, the פסוק about the קרבן for מעילה.

phrases.english: to exclude one who acts intentionally.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף רַב פָּפָּא הֲדַר בֵּיהּ, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the תיובתא, adds that רב פפא himself retracted, and brings a ברייתא as background.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קרבן for מעילה applies only to one who sinned בשגגה, not במזיד.

steps.title: Why not derive the exemption by קל וחומר?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why a פסוק is needed. A קל וחומר seems to work: other sins punished by כרת exempt the מזיד from a קרבן, so מעילה, which has no כרת, should certainly exempt him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't this a logical conclusion? Other מצוות that carry כרת exempt one who sinned on purpose from a קרבן. So מעילה, which has no כרת, should surely exempt one who did it on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, a challenge is raised: we should not need a פסוק, because logic (a קל וחומר) gives the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic treats כרת as the more severe punishment. If even severe כרת-sins do not let a מזיד bring a קרבן, then the lighter sin of מעילה should not either. The point is that the פסוק would seem to be unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it logical? (introduces a proposed derivation)
Spiritual 'cutting off,' a severe punishment from Heaven
Exempts

phrases.english: But is it not a logical inference?

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה שְׁאָר מִצְוֹת שֶׁחַיָּיב בָּהֶן כָּרֵת —
phrases.english: Just as the other מצוות for which one is liable to karet —
(the Torah) exempts the intentional sinner (from an offering),
misuse, which has no karet —
is it not logical that it exempts the intentional sinner?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the פסוק cited in Step 22 is needed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from the more severe כרת-sins would already give the same rule.

steps.title: The קל וחומר fails because מעילה carries מיתה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects the קל וחומר. מעילה carries מיתה בידי שמים, which other sins lack, so it may be stricter in this way. That is why the פסוק is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: No! You can say this about other מצוות, which do not carry a death penalty. Can you say it about מעילה, which does carry a death penalty? So the פסוק says 'בשגגה' to exclude one who did it on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא knocks down the קל וחומר and concludes that the rule must come from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In one way מעילה is more severe than other sins, because it carries מיתה בידי שמים. So we cannot assume it is lighter. Since logic fails, the word 'בשגגה' is what teaches that a מזיד brings no קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (this about X), (can you say it about Y?)
Death penalty (here, at the hands of Heaven)
Therefore the פסוק teaches

phrases.english: No! If you say so regarding the other מצוות,
for which (the Torah) did not impose death,
will you say so regarding misuse,
for which (the Torah) imposed death!
phrases.notes: This is מיתה בידי שמים, death at the hands of Heaven.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse states: 'through error' —
to exclude one who acts intentionally.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר of Step 23.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: מעילה is not lighter in every way, because it carries מיתה בידי שמים, which other כרת-sins lack.

steps.title: The תנא seems inconsistent about which punishment is more severe
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק points out that the תנא first treats כרת as more severe, but then treats מיתה as more severe.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said to רב חייא בר אבין: This תנא at first considered כרת stronger, and at the end considered מיתה stronger!
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא points out a contradiction inside the ברייתא. This sets up an explanation that will follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proposed קל וחומר (Step 23) assumed that כרת is more severe than מעילה. The rejection (Step 24) assumed that מיתה, which מעילה has, is more severe. The ברייתא seems to switch which punishment it treats as the more serious one.

keyTerms.meaning: At first, originally
He considers it stronger / more severe
In the end

steps.confusionAlert: Both halves of the ברייתא are about the same sin, מעילה. The problem is only that its two arguments rank כרת and מיתה in opposite orders.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
phrases.english: And Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said to him,
to Rav Ḥiyya bar Avin:
This tanna, at first,
considers karet stronger,
and in the end considers death stronger!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי תַּנָּא מֵעִיקָּרָא אַלִּימָא לֵיהּ כָּרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the internal consistency of the ברייתא from Steps 22 to 24.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The קל וחומר treats כרת as more severe, while its rejection treats מיתה as more severe. These two rankings contradict each other.

steps.title: The stringency of מעילה is about the minimum amount, not the type of punishment
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אבין explains that the ברייתא's rejection of the קל וחומר is not ranking מיתה above כרת. It points to something else: for מעילה you are liable for מיתה even for less than a כזית, while for other prohibitions there is no punishment below a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he (רב חייא בר אבין) said to him (רב נחמן בר יצחק): This is what the ברייתא means: 'No! You can say this about the other מצוות, because there you are not liable for מיתה for less than a כזית. Can you say the same about מעילה, where you are liable for מיתה even for less than a כזית?'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חייא בר אבין answers רב נחמן בר יצחק's contradiction. He re-reads the ברייתא's words so they no longer say that מיתה is more severe than כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contradiction only existed because we thought the ברייתא was saying 'מיתה is worse than כרת.' Now the stringency of מעילה is about the minimum amount: מעילה punishes even below a כזית, and other prohibitions do not. So כרת can stay the more severe punishment, and the ברייתא no longer contradicts itself.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means. Used to re-read a statement in a new way.
An olive's volume. The standard minimum amount for liability when eating something forbidden.
With less than an olive's volume.
The other מצוות, meaning the other prohibitions that carry כרת.
Death at the hands of Heaven. This is the punishment for intentional מעילה.

steps.confusionAlert: רב חייא בר אבין is not saying that מעילה is a more severe sin than the כרת sins. He is saying that מעילה has one special feature, liability for a tiny amount, which could make you think it is stricter in this one respect.

phrases.english: And he said to him: This is what he (the Tanna) is saying:
phrases.notes: The speaker is רב חייא בר אבין, answering רב נחמן בר יצחק.

phrases.english: No! If you say this about the rest of the מצוות,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן לֹא חִיֵּיב בָּהֶן מִיתָה בְּפָחוֹת מִכְּזַיִת,
phrases.english: it is because for them [the Torah] did not make one liable to death for less than an olive's volume,
would you say the same about misuse of sacred property,
for which [the Torah] made one liable to death even for less than an olive's volume?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised by רב נחמן בר יצחק in Step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading of the ברייתא: the stringency is the minimum amount, not the severity of the punishment.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to treat מיתה as more severe than כרת, which contradicts its first claim that כרת is more severe.
steps.terutzMaskana: כרת stays more severe. The ברייתא only means that מעילה is unusually strict because liability applies even below a כזית.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק accepts the answer
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק thanks רב חייא בר אבין and says the answer has put his mind at ease.
steps.simpleTranslation: He (רב נחמן בר יצחק) said to him: May your mind be at rest, just as you have put my mind at rest.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק accepts רב חייא בר אבין's answer and blesses him for it. For a moment, the problem seems solved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a warm acceptance of the answer, phrased as a blessing. It is only a pause, though. The next line will show that the answer has a serious weakness.

keyTerms.meaning: May your mind be at rest. A blessing of thanks.
For you have put my mind at rest.

phrases.english: And he said to him: May your mind be at rest,
phrases.notes: The speaker is רב נחמן בר יצחק.

phrases.english: for you have put my mind at rest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The person who asked the question accepts the answer from Step 26.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For now, the answer seems to resolve the contradiction in the ברייתא.

steps.title: רבה and רב שׁשת already attacked this answer
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אבין warns that his answer is not really comforting, because רבה and רב שׁשת rejected it. He begins to quote their challenge: 'Who did you hear that holds...'
steps.simpleTranslation: He (רב חייא בר אבין) said to him: What comfort is there here? רבה and רב שׁשת threw an axe at it (rejected it): Whom have you heard who says...
steps.whatsHappening: רב חייא בר אבין tells רב נחמן בר יצחק not to relax, because his own answer was already attacked. This line sets up a challenge whose full content continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer depends on a specific rule: that you are liable for מיתה for מעילה even below a כזית. רבה and רב שׁשת ask which תנא actually holds that rule. Their goal is to show that this rule may not fit the תנא of our ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: What comfort is there? What is settling about this?
They threw an axe at it. An idiom meaning they strongly attacked or rejected it.
Whom have you heard who says...? A challenge asking which תנא holds a certain view.

steps.confusionAlert: It is surprising that the person attacking the answer is the same רב חייא בר אבין who just gave it. He is honestly reporting that greater scholars rejected his explanation.

phrases.english: And he said to him: What comfort is there?
phrases.notes: The speaker is רב חייא בר אבין.

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבָּה וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת שָׁדוּ בֵּיהּ נַרְגָּא:
phrases.english: For Rabba and Rav Sheshet threw an axe at it (rejected it):
Whom have you heard who says
